summary: FuturePathways Inc. has built eco-friendly travel into its operations through a green travel policy, a commuter reward program, a gradual shift to an electric vehicle fleet, and partnerships with eco-certified vendors. Executives pledge sustainable travel, virtual meeting technology is expanded, and employee training supports the effort. The company plans an annual environmental impact assessment to track results and set new targets.
one_line: FuturePathways Inc. adopts a comprehensive green travel policy with rewards, EV fleet, eco-certified partners, teleconferencing, training, and annual impact assessments.
key_facts: FuturePathways Inc. implemented its comprehensive green travel policy effective October 15, 2023, under sustainability officer Evan Greenwald.
The green travel policy prioritizes teleconferencing over long-distance travel, gives incentives for eco-friendly transportation, and partners with green hotels and service providers.
The Green Commuter Reward Program began September 7th 2023 and rewards cycling, walking and public transit commuting with green credits.
Green credits can be redeemed for extra vacation days or vouchers for health and wellness programs.
On November 20, 2023, FuturePathways Inc. unveiled a plan to gradually replace its corporate fleet with electric vehicles; Alexei Petrov helped select the fleet.

CEO Julia Martins and her executive team pledged to use sustainable travel methods on all business-related trips, including EVs, airlines with carbon offset programs, and eco-certified accommodations.

Helena Gimenez of procurement management oversees partnerships with eco-certified hotels and travel providers offering sustainability certifications, waste reduction programs and energy efficiency measures.
IT director Marco Silva said virtual meetings reduce carbon footprint, save time and allow greater scheduling flexibility.

Workshops and training sessions since September 10, 2023 are led by the Environment and Sustainability Committee, chaired by Dr. Lorraine Fisher, covering energy conservation, waste reduction and biodiversity preservation.
FuturePathways plans an annual environmental impact assessment measuring carbon emission reductions, Green Commuter Reward Program participation rates and employee feedback.
Samantha Cho, Director of Human Resources, said the team responded enthusiastically to the rewards program and is experiencing a cultural shift towards sustainability.
Evan Greenwald said: "It's not about cutting costs; it's about taking responsibility for our planet."
